summary: AI agent given a measurable task and a code setup; runs autonomous experiment loops overnight (modify → train/eval → keep/discard). Self-improving via metric-driven feedback without human intervention. 21k stars, March 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the pattern of autonomous improvement loops is interesting for skill distillation, but AgentForge's deterministic state machine and sequential pipeline are a deliberate design choice. Prompt-self-evolution is a flagged red-flag pattern. HID-188 covers run-outcome memory. Backlog gate triggered (11 open issues).

summary: Proposes compiling raw knowledge sources once into a persistent, interlinked Markdown wiki rather than re-running RAG at query time. 5k stars in two weeks. Inspired wave of open-source implementations.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge's skill distillation agent already compiles run artifacts into structured, reusable skills. The wiki pattern adds cross-reference and contradiction detection which doesn't map cleanly to the orchestration domain. Executor skills gap (noted in architecture doc) is tracked by HID-188.

summary: OpenAI shipped managed Agents API into public beta Sep 10 2026. Handles orchestration, long-running sessions, context compaction, sub-agent coordination, and crash recovery server-side. No extra fee beyond tokens.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge is its own orchestrator with a deterministic state machine; adopting a managed external service would replace rather than enhance it. Context compaction patterns are interesting but AgentForge's CLI subprocess model doesn't use a managed API layer.

summary: LangGraph 2.0 (Feb 2026) codified three years of production patterns; 1.2.11 (Aug 2026) shipped checkpoint fixes. Key features: built-in checkpointing saving full graph state after every node execution, cross-session memory, fault recovery.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge already has an explicit stateMachine.ts with deterministic transitions, artifact model, and idempotencyRepository. Checkpointing patterns are covered conceptually by HID-186 (partial retry via earliest-failure-point detection). No new gap.

summary: ByteDance's open-source super-agent harness that orchestrates sub-agents, persistent memory, sandboxes, and extensible skills. Hit #1 GitHub Trending after v2.0 release in Sep 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — shares architectural DNA with AgentForge (CLI agents, skill memory, deterministic stages) but oriented toward multi-model parallelism which AgentForge deliberately defers. No specific gap identified that isn't already tracked in open issues.

summary: Kanban-style multi-agent team system supporting 200+ models across 75+ providers. Trending on GitHub in September 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — parallel multi-agent execution is explicitly deferred in AgentForge (sequential determinism is a design choice). The cross-provider routing is already partially handled by role-tier model routing shipped in foundry/src/config/agentModels.ts.

summary: Practical patterns, starters, and CLI tools for orchestrating agents with audit, init, and cost tooling. Trending on GitHub September 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — cost/audit tooling theme is already tracked by HID-163 (per-run token cost and stage latency telemetry). No new gap.

summary: Proposes 7-layer memory architecture for autonomous AI agents inspired by neuroscience: sensory buffer, working memory, episodic memory, semantic memory, procedural memory, meta-memory, and prospective memory.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — episodic and procedural memory layers are relevant to HID-188. However the full 7-layer architecture is speculative and far exceeds AgentForge's current needs. Too complex for 1-2 agent runs. Backlog gate triggered regardless.

summary: Survey paper on persistent memory, state management, and governance in LLM agents. Covers cross-session memory, stale-memory resolution, and governance patterns across 200+ production runs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — governance and cross-run stale memory patterns are directly relevant. HID-188 (episodic memory injection) and HID-183 (stale-run health monitor) already track the most applicable themes. No new gap identified.

source: DARWIN: Dynamic Agentically Rewriting Self-Improving Network
summary: Proposes agents that dynamically rewrite their own network weights and prompts via an agentic feedback loop. Self-evolution through architecture mutation and reward-driven selection.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — prompt self-evolution and RL training loops are explicitly red-flagged as disqualifying patterns in AgentForge's evaluation criteria. The gap this addresses (adaptive prompts) is partly covered by skill distillation already shipped.

source: State of AI Agent Memory 2026 Report (mem0.ai)
summary: Benchmark and trends report covering episodic, semantic, and procedural memory performance across production agent deployments. Cross-session contradiction rate ~1-in-12 sessions without proper memory layering.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — confirms real production pain around stale/contradicting memories. Reinforces HID-188's priority but doesn't introduce new patterns beyond what's already tracked. The executor-skills gap (executor prompts don't receive distilled skills) noted in architecture docs is the most actionable finding but is already scoped in HID-188.
